hook_text: 21 367 runners. Is that about 21 365, 21 370, 21 400 or 21 000? All four. Here is why.
clip_script: A fun run in Durban: 21 367 runners. Nearest 5? Numbers ending in 0 or 5. 21 367 sits between 21 365 and 21 370. Two steps back, three steps forward. 21 365. Nearest 10? Look at the units, 7. Up. 21 370. Nearest 100? Look at the tens, 6. Up. 21 400. Nearest 1 000? Look at the hundreds, 3. Down. 21 000. One crowd, four answers, and the question decides. Now the shop: fridge R6 748, stove R4 395. Round to the nearest R1 000: R7 000 plus R4 000 is R11 000. Exact: R11 143. Close, so it makes sense. Round first, then calculate.
visual_style: A number line zooming in from thousands to hundreds to tens to fives, with 21 367 jumping to the nearest mark each time.
mood: Energetic, like a race commentator calling the finish.
pacing: Four quick roundings of one number, then the shop estimate, then the one-line rule.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and round the price of something in your kitchen to the nearest 5, 10 and 100.
